quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Makes you more visible to other drivers.
Should only be used at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your helmet makes you more visible to other drivers day and night.

questions.question: If there are hazards on your left, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.explanation: Ride on the right side of your lane when hazards are on your left. Change your position as road conditions change.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes on a motorcycle?

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Slow down to let vehicles pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone cannot show everything behind you.

questions.question: When will a helmet NOT provide the best protection?
questions.explanation: A helmet with cracks cannot protect you properly. Your helmet should be DOT certified, fit snugly, and be free of damage.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers?
questions.explanation: Most conflicts happen at intersections. Ride carefully and stay alert when approaching or entering intersections.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane before passing another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane to get the best view before passing. This gives you the clearest view of the road ahead.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane
It is better than going slowly
You will stay in your lane
It is safe because motorcycles are small

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before turning.

questions.question: What should you do when riding over rough surfaces?
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly to keep control of your motorcycle on rough surfaces.

questions.question: Which sign is typically rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. They show the rules you must follow on that road.

questions.question: On a motorcycle with a sidecar, where should the passenger sit?

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Limiting the distance ridden in one day

questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest. Do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Do not use artificial stimulants, as you will feel tired and unsafe when they wear off.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: You will be slowing down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has only one brake light, which is harder to see than a car's two brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing down quickly so other drivers notice it sooner.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.explanation: Check that your clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is OPEN, not closed.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars appear:
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle should:

options.text: Allow the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
Have a seat even with the rider's waist.
Have a seat that is 10 inches above the rider's waist.
Have a seat that is 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can reach the ground while you sit on the seat. Keep your feet on the footrests while riding.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, which is NOT a potential hazard?

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the vehicle's mirrors hitting you, wind gusts, and objects thrown by passengers. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as closely as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: The best way to be seen at an intersection is to ride with your headlight on. Always keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: Your lane position should do everything EXCEPT:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Increase your ability to be seen by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, keeps you out of blind spots, avoids road hazards, protects your lane, shows your intentions, protects you from wind gusts, and gives you an escape route. It should never make you harder to see.

questions.question: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve your view of cross traffic.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve your view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign. Then move forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean your body forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to see if traffic is coming. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. It is recommended for all riders. Loose clothing can catch on the motorcycle. Passengers should lean with the operator during turns. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only in slippery conditions.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use if used correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use if used correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes anytime you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn the location of all controls before you ride.

questions.question: If using a sidecar to transport a load, you should:

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not shift and affect handling. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping up during sudden left turns.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone consumed eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed to estimate remaining alcohol. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.
